cells.tense: You are here with the thread and the aim in the same pair of hands.
cells.act: spend an hour with the thing you love without a task attached to it
cells.ask: Take an hour with something you love, attach no task to it, and keep the direction sitting quietly beside you the whole way.
cells.core:
You can follow a thought down through its pattern until it opens out, which most people cannot do without losing the thread they came in with. The direction holds while you go, and it is still in your hands when you come back up. Depth and drive are running together for you here.

What keeps this honest is under the work, in the quiet. So take an hour with something you love and put no task on it, no notes, no return. The aim will be there when the hour ends, and it will be carrying more of you than it is now. This is not a break from where you are pointed — it is the part that keeps the pointing true, and it does not need to produce anything.

cells.tense: You are going to trace the whole design before the first real move is made.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Before anyone asks, say the shape of the plan out loud in one clear pass, then leave it stated and stop refining it.
cells.core:
The depth is real, and it has started getting out in front of the doing. Pattern under pattern gets traced before anything has been tried, and the aim keeps sliding out of reach while the tracing goes on. What was precision is turning into a way of not beginning.

One plain move breaks it. Say the shape of the thing out loud, once, early, in front of whoever needs it — not another analysis, the frame itself, stated plainly. It will sound smaller out loud than it did in your head, and smaller is what this needs. Then leave it be instead of taking another pass, and the design you have already worked out becomes something you can walk rather than re-draw.
cells.sheetLine: You sketch the whole design before the first move. Say it plainly, once.

cells.tense: You set out toward a destination, and you are still standing at the door.
cells.act: share the joy with the people it belongs to
cells.ask: Bring one good thing that happened this week to the ones who share it with you, and say it out loud while it is still fresh.
cells.core:
The drive toward the destination has gone thin. The depth is still there — you can take a thought down as far as it goes — but it does not turn into motion, and nothing arrives at the other end of it. You have settled into standing still and calling it patience.

Pushing harder will not bring the momentum back. Something lighter will. A good thing happened this week, and it belongs to the people you were with when it did. Say it out loud to them while it is still fresh. That is the whole instruction. Gladness shared with the people it came from is what gets a quiet line moving again. It will not feel like progress. It is the start of it.
cells.sheetLine: You set out and stayed at the door. Say the good thing out loud.

cells.tense: You are steering toward something right now and saying it steers itself.
cells.act: rest in the connection without doing anything with it
cells.ask: Sit with someone close to you once, with no plan and no purpose, and do nothing with the time — let the company be the whole of it.
cells.core:
You are the one holding the direction. The ones near you move because you have quietly kept the line, and if your version is the version on the table, the aim was obvious or belonged to the room. The steering is yours. No one has been told, and you would not call it work.

Before you were carrying anyone anywhere, you liked being near people for no reason at all. Go back to that. Sit with someone you are close to and do nothing with the time — no plan, no fixing, no steering. Let the company be the whole of it. That is the simpler form of what you do, and it is yours whether or not anyone says so.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the direction and say it holds itself. Just sit with someone.
